floor_history.headline: MoveImage floor 21 -> 7 and build_insns 47 -> 49 (== target): hoisting `D_8009BF28 = packed;` to be the first primitive store puts `sll $v0,$s1,16` at the head of the post-guard block, so reorg's eage

MoveImage floor 7 -> 2 (build_insns 49 == target): walking the rect argument with a post-increment pointer hoists the rect[0] read ahead of the D_8009BF28 store WITHOUT losing the H2 delay-slot steal;
Found the mechanism behind the whole floor-2 residual: p[6] is MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (expr.c:4567) so sched.c:834-839 exempts it from the D_8009BF2C symbol store and it floats 4 slots early; re-spelling it

frontier.hypothesis: On the plain-argument base (candidate_alt_plain_arg.c, 4/49) the ONLY residual is the dev-table lui/lw pair being 4 slots late, caused by priority(insn 83) rising from 1 to 2 via a true memory dependence on the packet store that does not exist in the floor-2 build despite textually identical RTL for both insns. Removing that edge while keeping the plain dispatch-argument read should close the function.
frontier.mechanism: priority() is the longest weighted path from the block start (sched.c:1497); the dev-table load is placed early only while it is the lowest-priority ready insn. The new edge is a true store->load dependence from the packet store, which can only arise if canon_rtx stops resolving the packet pointer to its symbol -- so either the extra pseudo perturbs the REG_EQUAL/reg_n_sets bookkeeping in init_alias_analysis, or the two dumps were taken in different sched passes (post-RA there are no pseudos, so no pointer is ever resolved and every pointer store aliases every symbol load).
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS. Re-run both standalone dumps (tmp/grind/MoveImage/s3/mv.c and mv2.c) with BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1 and separate the sched1 and sched2 sections, then read `reg_n_sets` / the REG_EQUAL note on the packet-pointer set insn in each. Do NOT modify the compiler -- the diagnostics are already compiled in. Once the cause is known, look for a spelling that keeps the dispatch argument read plain while the packet store still canonicalizes to its symbol.

frontier.hypothesis: The MEM_IN_STRUCT_P lever applied to the OTHER dispatch read (`fn = p[2]`) interacts with the dev-table load's placement, and that cross-product is unmeasured.
frontier.mechanism: The fn load is also mem/s and therefore also alias-exempt from both symbol stores; making it plain gives it true dependences on the stores too, which changes both its own slot and the readiness order in which the dev-table load competes.
frontier.next_probe: STRUCTURAL. Cross sweep10's G4 (both dispatch reads walked) with each of sweep11's 11 dev-table placements, gated on build_insns == 49, and dump BB2_PRIO_DEBUG for any form whose score drops below 4.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining search space on both bases is a single scheduler edge with a two-number acceptance test, which fits a directed permuter campaign better than further hand enumeration.
frontier.mechanism: The acceptance test is score 0 with build_insns == 49 from one sandbox run, and the structural axis has now been swept ~90 forms deep by hand across three sessions.
frontier.next_probe: PERMUTER modality, seeded from BOTH memory/grind/MoveImage/candidate.c and memory/grind/MoveImage/candidate_alt_plain_arg.c, with a clean single-function target built from asm/funcs/MoveImage.s + tools/decomp-permuter/prelude.inc, PERM_* directives over the body statement order and the dispatch-read spelling, fresh-seed windows per permuter-fresh-seed-discipline, harvested in-turn. Every closing form is a PROPOSAL and must clear the 6-test cheat checklist plus the layer-1 reviewer.
